title: A five-minute tour of what a modern IMRC site could do
seeing: A working demo built with fictional Ramayana-era profiles — no real members, no real data, nothing is sent anywhere.
why: The board has asked how we bring members back, reach younger families, and make decisions with more of the community in the room. Each stop shows one answer.
presenterNote: Begin here before showing any member screens.

title: Every member belongs somewhere visible
seeing: IMRC National, the regional chapters, and the states and provinces each one serves — drawn from the member's own home-city field.
why: Members who can see their chapter, and see that other chapters exist, are far more likely to show up for their own and cross over to a neighbor's events.

title: One sign-in, one profile, one place for everything
seeing: A simulated sign-in. In production this becomes invitation-and-approval with real accounts; here it just opens a fictional member's world.
why: Today a member's registrations, votes, and family details live in email threads and spreadsheets. Once they live behind one sign-in, every later step in this tour becomes possible.

title: Every visit ends with a small next step
seeing: Rama's dashboard — a suggested introduction with the reason shown, an upcoming event two connections are attending, and a ways-to-help prompt.
why: Engagement is built from small repeated actions. A dashboard that always offers one easy, relevant thing to do turns occasional visitors into participants.

title: Suggestions members can trust
seeing: A recommended introduction and the plain reason for it — shared chapter, shared lineage, or shared interest.
why: New and returning members stay when they find people. Showing why someone is suggested keeps it feeling like a community, not an algorithm.

title: A living directory, not a printed one
seeing: Searchable, filterable members with lineage collections and directional relationships, and Rama's family and friends view.
why: Families join together and stay together. Letting a household see itself in the tree, and add a new family member in one step, is how the next generation gets an account at all.

title: Registration without the reply-all
seeing: Rama registered his household for this event. The panel updated after saving, and the event can be added to any calendar with one download.
why: Every extra step between ‘I saw the event’ and ‘I'm registered’ loses people. One panel, whole household, calendar file — and organizers get a real count instead of guesses.

title: Plan the whole convention from a phone
seeing: The four-day OKC 2028 programme filtered by day and category — business, charity, RAYS, Sakhi, culture, meals — and Rama's selected sessions.
why: Attendance at conventions is decided months earlier, when a member either can or cannot picture their weekend. Registration, hotel link, flights, airport coach, and agenda in one flow removes the reason to put it off.

title: Participation you can see — and nobody else has to
seeing: A session QR code, a recorded check-in, and the badge it unlocked. Badges are private; there is no public score or leaderboard.
why: Recognition drives repeat attendance. Keeping it private keeps it healthy — encouragement without competition, and organizers finally know who actually walked in.

title: Decisions with the whole community in the room
seeing: A chapter poll Rama has already answered, and the national and chapter officer ballots — President, Vice President, Treasurer, Secretary — linked from the calendar event.
why: Turnout for decisions is the most honest measure of engagement we have. A ballot that reaches every member's phone, with the calendar reminder pointing back to it, will outperform any proxy form.

title: Members helping members
seeing: Questions and replies, mentoring offers, requests for help, and spotlight nominations — all browser-local in this demo.
why: Communities that only broadcast lose people; communities that let members contribute keep them. This is where the newer member finds a mentor and the veteran finds a reason to stay involved.

title: Where this stands, and what the board is being asked
seeing: Built and shown today: the member experience above, with fictional data stored only in this browser. Designed and reviewed, not yet turned on: real accounts, a private database, real registration and notifications, moderation, and administrator engagement insights.
why: The ask: approve the production phase so a pilot chapter can use this with real members.
presenterNote: Pause for the board's production-pilot discussion.
